density_challenge: The opposite case: this unit is closer to 'supporting' than 'standalone', because its strength is the wrong edition. Everything verified is solid text, but the three load-bearing mechanisms (hard-hat case, satisficing, three-element plan with backward 'why') are all from Chapter 1 of the 2023 second edition. The only Palantir evidence is one unexplained list item in Qureshi, whose own link (ASIN 193382011X, ISBN checksum verified) is the 2013 first edition, whose printed contents (see below) show a differently organized Chapter 1 with no 'High-Level Research Plan' section; so 'what new hires were sent' and 'what the video explains' do not overlap on any checked page. The hard-hat case is a single anecdote with no client, year or sample size, and its only outcome is that no product shipped, which is thin as a recurring 'example' beat. The describe/interpret/report/assess scheme is a label on form columns that the author never defines, and he says he usually skips the forms, so the strongest visual idea (the worksheet close-up) is an observation about a form, not a method the author teaches; the explorer correctly hedges, but 8 minutes of screen time on a hedged item is a lot. Two further risks: the Chinese 'commodity' rendering '大宗' and the overreach on '人人更爱新款' show the translation layer itself needs care, and many locators use a private 'clean draft' line numbering nobody else can reproduce. In favor of the explorer's verdict: the second-edition chapter, the author's own forms, and two long author interviews are all first-hand, every quote I checked is verbatim (34 of 34 ch1 quotes machine-matched), the limits are written in the author's own words, and a visible edition caveat on screen resolves the Palantir mismatch honestly. My recommendation is 'standalone only if framed as Portigal's method (2e Ch1 plus author-published forms) with the 2013-edition caveat on screen; otherwise supporting'. Also note: the six repo PDFs are tied to the first edition more firmly than the explorer states (see missed sources), which helps the Palantir-era link for forms and field guide, though not for the Chapter 1 content.
missed_sources: First-edition excerpt PDF from Rosenfeld Media, 'Interviewing-Users-Excerpt.pdf' (PDF created 2013-05-01, 18 pages), reachable through Internet Archive: https://web.archive.org/web/20150919113557id_/http://rosenfeldmedia.com/app/uploads/2014/10/Interviewing-Users-Excerpt.pdf?331fe5 (also 2013-10-17 and 2019-12-09 captures). It contains the full 1e print table of contents (ch1 sections, ch5 'A Guide to Participating in Fieldwork' p.69, ch7 'Debriefing After the Interview' p.115 with 'Taking Field Notes' and 'Sharing Field Highlights', ch9 'Create a Topline Report' p.137) plus 1e Chapter 3 pp.36-46 (recruiting, screener, field guide with 'Give out release form and get signature / Turn on video camera / Confirm timing' and 'Remember, this is not a script'). This is the Palantir-era text the explorer lacked; it shows hard hat, satisficing and pain-point passages are not in it, and ties the screener, interview guide, participation guide, debrief and topline PDFs to the first edition's chapters. The explorer's gap list says 1e text was not obtained.
